results.question: Will a late EMI affect my credit score?
results.answer: Yes — repayments are reported to credit bureaus every month, and an EMI paid late is reported as overdue for the days it was late even if you pay it later in the same month [KB-L-08]. If an auto-debit failed but you paid within the lender’s retry window before the reporting date, it will not be reported as overdue [KB-L-08]. If the debit failed due to insufficient funds there may also be a bounce charge as described in the failed-payment rules [PAY-2.1]. If you think a late/failed payment was reported or charged incorrectly, I can help raise a dispute for you to correct bureau data or charges [DSP-1.1].

results.question: When rates go up, can I extend my tenure instead of paying a higher EMI?
results.answer: Yes — when a floating-rate loan is reset you can ask to extend the tenure instead of increasing your EMI, subject to the product’s maximum tenure limits [KB-L-06]. By default we recalculate the EMI for the remaining tenure, but the borrower may request tenure extension at the reset and we notify you of every reset by SMS/email [LT-4.2][KB-L-06]. You may also have the one-time option to switch to a fixed rate at reset; check the KFS for any switch fee [KB-L-06]. If you want, I can check your floating loan’s next reset and show the effect of extending tenure — shall I do that?
